correctness.rationale: For identical positive rows, every agent projects onto one common median interval. Its endpoint agents remain fixed and all other agents approach them from the same side, proving interval invariance. The scalar update solves exactly and supplies the limit gap. Under iid continuous opinions, the rank ordering is uniform and each balanced subset determines a disjoint cut event of probability 1/binom(n,|S|). Uniform order-statistic gaps are Beta(1,n) independently of ranking; the exact survival and mean follow. Reduction to integer PARTITION and the converse NP membership use the same equality certificate. Reproduction program verify_rankone.py passed 3267 exact interval/orbit cases and 1089 exact probability/permutation cases; computations are not used to prove the all-size theorem.

originality.rationale: The surviving model-specific theorem is the frozen common-row median interval, full heterogeneous-rate discrete-time orbit and exact initial-distribution-weighted polarization gap law. Closest published general convergence and consensus theorems, and older asynchronous hardness and continuous-time median work, do not explicitly establish these precise quantified statements. Existing consensus-possibility and one-WA consequences are credited as already implied. Residual uncertainty about historic rank-one special cases remains.

General consensus-possibility and single averaging-agent results are prior implications and cannot themselves constitute the new contribution.

value.rationale: Rank-one positive influence is the natural globally shared-attention model of social opinion formation. The exact trajectories and the distribution of the ultimate disagreement diameter resolve an observable model outcome the general convergence theorem leaves unspecified; they quantify influence-weight imbalance, show an exact parity transition for uniform attention, and reveal arithmetic complexity even on a fully connected support graph. The Beta mixture supplies the entire distribution rather than a small numerical refinement. The auxiliary effect of one averaging agent provides direct comparative interpretation, while remaining credited to existing theory.
